# utils/scripts/quarantine-ledger.txt — the findings of the quarantine plugin in each file, kind and entity.
#
# utils/scripts/check-quarantine-ratchet.py generates each row of this file.  Do not edit a row by
# hand.  The test quarantine_ratchet reads the section .crucible.quarantine of each object of the
# target all, and it counts each distinct finding one time.  A count above its row fails the test,
# because a change can only lower a count (rule R11 of misc/01_10_2026_quarantine.md).  So a change
# that removes std::vector from a file and adds std::map to it fails.  A file that the ledger does
# not hold and that has a finding fails too: a new file has no finding.  A count below its row also
# fails, until the same commit writes the rows again:
#     python3 utils/scripts/check-quarantine-ratchet.py --build-dir build --write
# On a merge conflict in this file, take the version of main, build, and write the rows again.
#
# THE ROWS
#   format 4                       The format of the rows.
#   configuration NAME KEY VALUE   A build that counts: the build kind and the target tier of
#                                  utils/scripts/build_target.py, and each cache variable that changes
#                                  the objects of all or their preprocessor arms.  NAME is the build
#                                  kind, with -bench and -fuzz for those options.  The first
#                                  configuration is the base.
#   FILE KIND COUNT ENTITY         The number of findings of the kind KIND and the entity ENTITY in
#                                  the file, in the base configuration.  ENTITY is the rest of the
#                                  line.  The head comment of utils/tools/quarantine/quarantine.cpp
#                                  gives the kinds, and THE ENTITY of
#                                  utils/scripts/check-quarantine-ratchet.py gives the entity of each
#                                  kind.  The entity holds no line, so a move of code keeps each row.
#   NAME FILE KIND DELTA ENTITY    The count of the configuration NAME, as a difference from the
#                                  base count (+N or -N).
#
# THE OPT-OUT REGIONS
#   A finding inside an opt-out region has the kind opted_out, and its entity is "REASON | KIND
#   ENTITY": the reason of the region, and the kind and the entity of the finding.  So these rows
#   hold what each region covers.  A region that covers more fails the test until
#       python3 utils/scripts/check-quarantine-ratchet.py --build-dir build --write --admit
#   writes the new count.  Use --admit only for a region of a reason class of CLAUDE.md section
#   XXII, and give the reason in the commit.  The test budget_history gives a warning for each such
#   count on each run.  utils/scripts/quarantine-region-ledger.txt holds the regions themselves.
#
# THE TIER
#   The tier names the target of the build flags.  When a compile of the objects of all has its own
#   -march=native or -mcpu=native, the tier adds "+" and the native tier of the host.  The units of
#   test/layer/admitted_flag_matrix compile with the release flags, and each bench target adds
#   -march=native, so each x86_64 configuration here has the native tier of the build host.  A
#   build on another processor can compile other preprocessor arms, for example the AVX-512 arm of
#   include/crucible/SwissTable.h, so the check does not apply to it.
#
# THE CONFIGURATIONS
#   x86_64-debug-asan              The default preset, in the build directory build.  The base.
#   x86_64-release                 The release preset (build-release).
#   x86_64-debug-asan-bench-fuzz   The default preset with CRUCIBLE_BENCH=ON and CRUCIBLE_FUZZ=ON:
#                                      cmake --preset default -B build-extended -DCRUCIBLE_BENCH=ON
#                                      -DCRUCIBLE_FUZZ=ON
#                                  The CI job fuzz builds it.
#   aarch64-...                    The default and the release preset on aarch64.  Only CI builds
#                                  them.  The leg prints the rows of its configuration after a failed
#                                  check and when the ledger does not hold it, and --import LOG puts
#                                  them here.
#   A change that lowers a count in each configuration writes only the base rows.  A change of a
#   file or an arm that only a later configuration compiles writes that configuration too, with
#   --write in its build directory.  A change of the keys of the base generates this file again:
#   keep this head, remove the rows, and run --write --add-configuration in the build of each
#   configuration, the base first.
#   The vessel units that need PyTorch compile only when TORCH_DIR is set.  No configuration sets
#   TORCH_DIR, so the check does not apply to such a build, and the ledger does not count those
#   units.
format 4
